description: Post-DSE stream/I/O overlay. Packed SIMD streams, Crow ram_2p, flattened pe_kj. PE_NUM/SIMD/pack_bits come from the per-kernel recipe (16x4 ap_uint<128> is only autosa_mm). Not mixed into flash or DSE skills.

skills.pattern: working multi-PE x SIMD GEMM still uses bulk local_A[I][K] with sequential load then compute then store. Or a stream PE whose compute_j is II=4 because Crow[J] was complete-partitioned (mux_case_0). Or a stream PE at II=1 but ~7k cycles because LOOP_FLATTEN off restarts compute_j 16 times.
skills.strategy: Keep the autosa_mm ABI. Replace full-matrix locals with PE_NUM mm_pe tasks (16 for locked mm, 32 for 32x8/getting_started/intel) plus loaders under DATAFLOW. Stream SIMD as ap_uint<pack_bits> from the recipe (128 default, 256 for 32x8). Crow[J] MUST be ram_2p BRAM (do not complete-partition Crow). Unpack SIMD to scalars. Flatten k×j into one pe_kj pipeline of (K/SIMD)*J beats; do not use LOOP_FLATTEN off. Do not DEPENDENCE inter false. Fuse init/drain into pe_kj. Name the PE function mm_pe not PE.
required_steps: keep the exact extern C top name, parameter list, array ranks/shapes, and all existing #pragma HLS INTERFACE lines
include <hls_stream.h> and <ap_int.h>; typedef ap_uint<pack_bits> (128 for 16x4, ap_uint<256> for 32x8)
pack/unpack SIMD floats with ap_uint bit slices into scalars; never stream a struct of floats
declare static task functions with INLINE off: load_A, load_B, mm_pe, drain_B, store_C
DATAFLOW region contains only function calls and stream declarations
instantiate PE_NUM explicit mm_pe() calls (16 for mm/hcl_intel, 32 for 32x8/getting_started/intel/hcl/int16, 8 for catapult) plus load_A, load_B, drain_B, store_C
each mm_pe has private Crow[J] with BIND_STORAGE ram_2p bram; NEVER ARRAY_PARTITION Crow complete
one pe_kj loop of (K/SIMD)*J beats (1024 at SIMD=4 J=64, 512 at SIMD=8, 2048 at SIMD=2), PIPELINE II=1; do not use LOOP_FLATTEN off; do not DEPENDENCE inter false
fuse init/drain: first k-tile acc=partial, last k-tile fifo_C.write(acc); do not flatten pe_i0 when tile_loop=inside_tasks
if recipe tile_loop=around_dataflow (I/PE_NUM>1): pe_i0 wraps DATAFLOW in the TOP; mm_pe/load_B/drain_B have only pe_kj
PE_NUM and SIMD come from the recipe; do not name a function PE if a PE macro exists
guards: ARRAY_PARTITION complete on Crow[J] muxes Crow[j] into mux_case_0 → II=4, DSP=5 per PE
struct-of-floats or four fifo.read() of data_t inside the MAC loop also forces II>=4
LOOP_FLATTEN off on nested pe_k0/compute_j restarts a depth-35 pipeline 16 times → ~7070 PE cycles vs rank1 4228
DEPENDENCE inter false on flattened Crow is a lie (true dep at distance 64) and can mis-schedule
array of hls::stream must be ARRAY_PARTITION complete
do not clone AutoSA's 1000+ line PE/IO interconnect
DSP after csynth must stay near the recipe (float PE*SIMD*5, uint16 PE*SIMD, uint32 ~PE*SIMD*3). DSP~80 with PE=16 float means compute_j II=4 — revise
I/PE_NUM=2 with the i-tile loop inside mm_pe/load_B serializes two pe_kj trips (~4307 cycles). Rank1 ~2194 is ping-pong around DATAFLOW, not dual-MAC

skills.pattern: bulk memcpy of A/B/C into on-chip arrays then compute; or m_axi RMW of C inside the PE loop.
skills.strategy: Make DRAM access DATAFLOW tasks that burst into packed ap_uint<128> FIFOs. Keep A gmem0, B gmem1, C gmem2. Compute never touches m_axi.
required_steps: load_A and load_B are INLINE-off tasks that only pack and write streams
store_C only reads fifo_C and writes C[][]
do not allocate local_A[I][K] or local_B[J][K] in the top kernel
keep existing m_axi bundles so A/B/C can move in parallel
STREAM depth on fifo_C at least J (64); A/B depth >= 8
guards: ping-pong of a full local_A[I][K] inside one kernel call does not overlap DRAM with the same compute
do not read C from DRAM; autosa_mm gold is C=sum A*B from 0
never ARRAY_PARTITION the top-level m_axi ports

skills.pattern: B is fully buffered on-chip and broadcast to an unrolled PE loop inside one function.
skills.strategy: Stream packed vec4_bits along a PE chain. Always forward; drain_B consumes fifo_B[PE_NUM]. Replay B across i0 tiles.
required_steps: hls::stream<vec4_bits> fifo_B[PE_NUM+1] complete-partitioned
load_B writes fifo_B[0] with schedule i0, k0, j matching every PE compute_j
each mm_pe forwards every B beat; last forwards to drain_B
do not broadcast B through a shared local_B[J][K]
A schedule is i0, k0, p (no j); mm_pe reuses the A vec across compute_j
guards: mismatched load vs PE trip counts deadlock DATAFLOW streams
always forward and always drain
B layout is B[J][K]

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW on shared local_A/B/C; AutoSA clone; struct-of-floats SIMD FIFOs; Crow[J] ARRAY_PARTITION complete causing mux_case_0 II=4; or LOOP_FLATTEN off on pe_k0 causing 16 pipeline refills (~7k cycles).
skills.strategy: Reject shared on-chip A/B/C across DATAFLOW tasks. Reject AutoSA netlist clone. Reject struct-of-floats SIMD FIFOs. Reject complete-partition of Crow on the pipelined J index. Reject LOOP_FLATTEN off on nested k/j. If DSP is ~80 or II>1 with mux_case_0, Crow was muxed — use ram_2p. If PE is ~7k with II=1, k/j was not flattened — use pe_kj of 1024 beats.
required_steps: scan for local_A[I][K] used by more than one task — reject
scan for ARRAY_PARTITION variable=Crow complete — reject
scan for #pragma HLS LOOP_FLATTEN off — reject
scan for DEPENDENCE variable=Crow inter false — reject on flattened k×j
scan for hls::stream of a struct of four floats — reject
scan for kernel0, A_t16, B_t16 netlist clone — reject
require PE_NUM mm_pe() calls from the recipe, pe_kj II=1, DSP at recipe min_dsp (not a blanket DSP>>80 — that rejects int16 DSP=64 and catapult DSP=96)
guards: DATAFLOW on LCST body is not streamifying
do not complete-partition Crow on the pipelined J index
do not use LOOP_FLATTEN off; flatten k×j instead
struct-of-floats on the MAC loop is a separate II=4 failure mode
do not emit AutoSA 1600-line hls_baseline.cpp

skills.pattern: stream step that always emits PE_NUM=16, SIMD=4, ap_uint<128> float union pack, or gates success on DSP>=200. Wrong for int16 (DSP~64, pack 2xu16), catapult (PE=8, I_P, unsigned int), getting_started/intel (need 32 mm_pe calls, DSP~640), and the autosa_mm_32x8 overlay (PE=32 SIMD=8, ap_uint<256>, DSP~1280).
skills.strategy: Follow the mandatory PE recipe. Pack SIMD as ap_uint<pack_bits> with raw element bits. Float union is only for data_t float. pe_kj trip=(K/SIMD)*J. Instantiate PE_NUM explicit mm_pe calls. Architecture DSP floor is recipe min_dsp, not 200.
required_steps: typedef ap_uint<pack_bits> vec_bits where pack_bits is 256 (8xfloat 32x8), 128 (4xfloat or 4xu32), 64 (2xfloat), or 32 (2xu16)
integer pack: shift/mask data_t bits; never union {float f; unsigned u}
PE_NUM mm_pe() calls: 32 for 32x8/getting_started/intel/hcl/int16, 16 for mm/hcl_intel, 8 for catapult
pe_kj trip 512 at SIMD=8, 1024 at SIMD=4, or 2048 at SIMD=2 for J=64
if seed has bundle=gmem on A,B,C split to gmem0/gmem1/gmem2 so load_A/load_B/store_C can overlap
catapult loops and array ranks use I_P/J_P/K_P
guards: DSP>=200 as a universal stream gate rejects a correct int16 (64) or catapult (96) kernel
32 PE with 16 mm_pe() calls is still the 16x4 design
float pack on unsigned short fails csim
I/J/K on catapult does not compile

skills.pattern: PE_NUM=32 so I/PE=2, but the i-tile / ROWS_PER_PE loop is inside load_A, load_B, mm_pe, drain_B, store_C. Each DATAFLOW firing then does 2*pe_kj beats (~2048) and latency sticks at ~4307. Rank1 getting_started is ~2194; intel ~4178 is the same 32x4 class and is also hurt by inner-tile serialization.
skills.strategy: When the recipe says tile_loop=around_dataflow, wrap #pragma HLS DATAFLOW in the top i-tile loop (i0 += PE_NUM). Pass i0 into load_A/store_C. mm_pe, load_B, and drain_B have NO tile/i0/ROWS_PER_PE loop — one pe_kj of (K/SIMD)*J beats per firing. STREAM depth>=8 so the two tiles ping-pong. Dual-MAC two rows in one beat is not 32x8 (32x8 is SIMD=8 / ap_uint<256> / DSP~1280).
required_steps: top: for (int i0 = 0; i0 < I; i0 += PE_NUM) { #pragma HLS DATAFLOW ... }
load_A(A, fifo_A, i0) loads only rows i0..i0+PE_NUM-1; store_C writes the same rows
mm_pe / load_B / drain_B contain only pe_kj (or KTILES*J) — delete for tile < ROWS_PER_PE and for i0 += PE_NUM inside those tasks
STREAM depth fifo_B>=8, fifo_A>=KTILES, fifo_C>=J so ping-pong can overlap the two tiles
keep PE_NUM explicit mm_pe() calls and SIMD from the recipe (SIMD=4 pe_kj=1024, or SIMD=8 pe_kj=512 / ap_uint<256> for 32x8)
guards: tile loop inside tasks: II=1 at 640 DSP but latency ~4307 because two pe_kj trips are serialized in one DATAFLOW firing
two rows per beat at II=1 uses ~1280 DSP on a 32x4 design — that is dual-MAC, not the 32x8 overlay. 32x8 DSP~1280 is SIMD=8, not dual-MAC
DATAFLOW must be inside the i-tile loop; a DATAFLOW at function scope with inner tile loops is the miss
do not also keep pe_i0 inside mm_pe after wrapping DATAFLOW — that would replay 2x2 tiles
